possible_causes: Lithium-ion battery cell aging reduces charge retention and increases internal resistance, causing warmth and rapid discharge.
Faulty charging cables, debris in the charging port, or runaway background apps can mimic or accelerate battery wear.
safety_warnings: Do not attempt to pry open a sealed smartphone enclosure or puncture the battery.
If the back cover begins lifting, swelling, or emitting odor, stop using the device immediately.

recommended_initial_checks.title: Inspect battery usage and health settings
recommended_initial_checks.instructions: Open Settings > Battery to verify whether a single background application is causing abnormal drain and check the system-reported battery health indicator.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Test with a manufacturer-certified cable and adapter
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Disconnect third-party chargers and test charging using a known-good certified cable and power adapter connected directly to a wall outlet.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Restart the phone and check pending OS updates
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Perform a standard reboot and install pending operating system updates that resolve power management bugs.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Schedule authorized battery replacement
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: If battery health is degraded or unexpected shutdowns persist after software and charger checks, arrange replacement through an authorized service center.

records.escalation_requirements: Contact an authorized mobile repair technician if rapid drain or shutdowns continue after charger verification, or immediately if the device becomes too hot to hold.

related_symptoms: Battery swelling or back cover lift
possible_causes: Internal gas buildup from thermal or chemical degradation inside a lithium-ion battery cell.
safety_warnings: Stop using and charging the smartphone immediately.
Do not press, squeeze, bend, puncture, or attempt to remove a swollen lithium-ion battery.
Keep the device away from flammable materials and heat sources.

recommended_initial_checks.title: Unplug charger and power off the device
recommended_initial_checks.instructions: Safely unplug the charging cable from the wall outlet first, power off the phone if safe to touch, and place it on a non-flammable surface in a ventilated area.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Isolate the device in a cool, dry place
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Do not store the device in a pocket, bag, or near combustible surfaces. Avoid subjecting it to mechanical pressure.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Transport safely to an authorized repair or e-waste facility
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Contact an authorized service center or certified electronics recycler for safe battery containment and replacement.

records.escalation_requirements: Immediate qualified technician intervention is required. Do not continue operating or charging the device.
records.emergency_guidance: If the battery begins hissing, smoking, or catching fire, evacuate the immediate area and contact local emergency services.

related_symptoms: Constant loud or grinding fan noise
possible_causes: Blocked intake/exhaust air vents, dust accumulation on cooling fins, degraded fan bearings, or runaway background CPU load.
safety_warnings: Do not block bottom or side vents by using the laptop on soft fabrics such as beds or cushions.
Do not open the laptop chassis while connected to AC power.

recommended_initial_checks.title: Check external airflow and operating surface
recommended_initial_checks.instructions: Place the laptop on a flat, hard surface and verify that intake and exhaust vents are unobstructed.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Inspect CPU utilization for runaway processes
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Open Task Manager or Activity Monitor to check whether a stuck application or update process is holding CPU usage near 100%.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Switch to a balanced power profile
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Set system power mode to Balanced and observe whether fan speed and chassis temperature stabilize during light tasks.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Request professional internal cleaning and fan inspection
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: If grinding fan noise or thermal shutdowns persist, have a technician clean internal heatsinks, inspect the fan assembly, and refresh thermal compound.

records.escalation_requirements: Escalate to a qualified computer technician if thermal shutdowns continue, fan grinding is audible, or the chassis becomes painfully hot.

related_symptoms: Burning or chemical odor from vents
possible_causes: Shorted compressor winding, failing start capacitor, damaged power feed, or overloaded branch circuit.
safety_warnings: Stop operating the air conditioner immediately and leave the circuit breaker in the OFF position.
Do not repeatedly reset a tripping circuit breaker.
Do not open electrical access panels or touch internal capacitors or wiring.

recommended_initial_checks.title: Turn off unit controls and leave circuit disconnected
recommended_initial_checks.instructions: Switch the air conditioner off at the thermostat or remote control and keep the dedicated breaker off until inspected.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Ventilate the room if odor is present
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Open windows and avoid remaining in an enclosed room if a burning or chemical smell was detected.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Contact a licensed HVAC technician or electrician
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Schedule an on-site electrical insulation and compressor load inspection with a licensed HVAC professional.

records.escalation_requirements: Mandatory inspection by a licensed HVAC technician or certified electrician before restoring power.
records.emergency_guidance: If you see smoke, sparks, or smell persistent electrical burning after shutting off the breaker, evacuate and call emergency services immediately.

records.fault_category: Airflow Restriction or Low Cooling Efficiency
related_symptoms: Ice forming on coils or refrigerant lines
possible_causes: Clogged return air filters, incorrect thermostat mode, blocked outdoor condenser airflow, or low refrigerant charge.
safety_warnings: Turn the air conditioner off before inspecting or rinsing removable washable intake filters.
Do not attempt to handle refrigerant lines or pressurize the system yourself.

recommended_initial_checks.title: Verify thermostat mode and temperature setpoint
recommended_initial_checks.instructions: Confirm the unit is set to Cool mode (not Fan Only) with the setpoint at least 3°C below current room temperature.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Inspect and clean the removable air filter
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Power off the indoor unit, slide out the user-accessible washable dust filter per the owner's manual, rinse with clean water, and dry completely before reinstalling.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Check external clearance around the outdoor unit
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Visually confirm from a safe distance that leaves, debris, or objects are not blocking airflow around the outdoor condenser grille.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Book licensed HVAC refrigerant and coil check
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: If coil icing returns or warm air persists after cleaning the filter, schedule an HVAC technician to inspect refrigerant pressure and blower performance.

records.escalation_requirements: Contact a licensed HVAC technician if coils freeze repeatedly, cooling does not improve after filter cleaning, or unusual mechanical noises occur.

possible_causes: Blocked internal air vents, worn door gasket letting humid air enter, incorrect temperature dial setting, or defrost system malfunction.
safety_warnings: Do not use sharp metal tools to chip away frost or ice, as this can puncture refrigerant tubing.
Discard perishable food that has remained above safe storage temperature.

recommended_initial_checks.title: Verify temperature setting and internal vent clearance
recommended_initial_checks.instructions: Check that temperature controls are set to manufacturer defaults and ensure food containers are not blocking cold air vents between compartments.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Inspect door gasket alignment and cleanliness
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Wipe the rubber door seal with warm mild soapy water and verify the door closes flush all the way around without gaps.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Schedule appliance technician defrost & sealed-system check
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: If warm temperatures or heavy frost return within 24 hours, contact a qualified appliance technician to inspect the defrost heater, thermistor, and compressor.

records.escalation_requirements: Contact a certified appliance technician if compartment temperatures remain warm after verifying vents and door seals, or if repeated rear relay clicking occurs.

related_symptoms: Drum does not spin or agitate
possible_causes: Kinked external drain hose, lint or coins blocking the user-accessible drain filter trap, or a failing drain pump.
safety_warnings: Unplug the washing machine and keep the floor dry to prevent slipping or electrical shock.
Confirm water inside the drum has cooled before opening any front-access drain trap.

recommended_initial_checks.title: Inspect the external drain hose for kinks
recommended_initial_checks.instructions: Visually check the visible drain hose behind or beside the machine to confirm it is not crushed, kinked, or elevated above manufacturer height limits.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Clean the user-accessible coin trap filter (if equipped)
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: Unplug the machine, place a shallow tray and towel under the front service flap, and follow the owner's manual to clear coins or lint from the drain trap.

troubleshooting_steps.title: Contact an appliance technician for pump inspection
troubleshooting_steps.instructions: If the machine still fails to drain or displays a persistent pump error code, schedule professional service rather than disassembling internal electrical housings.

records.escalation_requirements: Contact a qualified appliance technician if drainage fails after checking the hose and accessible trap, or if water leaks onto the floor.
